Each case lists the two analytic IK solutions (q1, q2), in rad, for one reachable target. Choose what an honest IK routine should report. task.solution: Case 1: solution 1 is inside and solution 2 is inside the limits (after allowing 2π shifts), so: report both solutions. Case 2: solution 1 is inside and solution 2 is outside the limits (after allowing 2π shifts), so: report solution 1 only. Case 3: solution 1 is outside and solution 2 is outside the limits (after allowing 2π shifts), so: report no valid solution.
hints: A solution is admissible only if both of its joints satisfy their limits; a target being reachable by the arm does not make a solution admissible.

task.prompt: A planar 2R arm's joint 1 has the limit 2 ≤ q1 ≤ 5 rad. An IK routine returns raw angles in (-π, π]. A raw angle is admissible if it or the angle plus a whole number of turns (2π ≈ 6.2832) lies inside the limit. For each raw q1, decide whether it is inside or outside: 2.5, -1.5, 1.2, -0.9, 3.1, -0.3.
task.solution: 2.5 rad: nearest equivalent 2.5000 rad is inside. -1.5 rad: nearest equivalent 4.7832 rad is inside. 1.2 rad: nearest equivalent 1.2000 rad is outside. -0.9 rad: nearest equivalent 5.3832 rad is outside. 3.1 rad: nearest equivalent 3.1000 rad is inside. -0.3 rad: nearest equivalent 5.9832 rad is outside.
hints: The same configuration is described by q1, q1 + 2π and q1 - 2π; the limit window applies to the configuration, so test every equivalent value.
For each raw angle, add and subtract 2π (≈ 6.2832) and check whether any of the three values lies in the window.

2.5 rad: nearest equivalent 2.5000 rad is inside. -1.5 rad: nearest equivalent 4.7832 rad is inside. 1.2 rad: nearest equivalent 1.2000 rad is outside. -0.9 rad: nearest equivalent 5.3832 rad is outside. 3.1 rad: nearest equivalent 3.1000 rad is inside. -0.3 rad: nearest equivalent 5.9832 rad is outside.
task.remediation: Comparing only the raw value with the window wrongly rejects configurations such as a small negative angle whose 2π-equivalent is inside a window above π. Revisit joint limits in /lessons/R05, then practise a fresh X22 item before another independent check.

task.prompt: Planar 2R arm with relative joint angles (counter-clockwise positive; q1 is measured from the base +x axis, q2 from link 1), angles in radians, lengths in metres, everything in the base frame: l1 = 0.85 m, l2 = 1.15 m; tip position x = l1 cos q1 + l2 cos(q1 + q2), y = l1 sin q1 + l2 sin(q1 + q2). The target tip position is (x, y) = (-0.6, -1.2) m. Solve the inverse kinematics on the elbow branch with q2 < 0 (the elbow bends clockwise relative to link 1) and report q1 and q2. Angles are graded modulo 2π within ±0.001 rad; you may leave angles unwrapped.
task.solution: cos q2 = (x² + y² - l1² - l2²)/(2 l1 l2) = -0.1253, so q2 = -acos(cos q2) = -1.6964 rad. q1 = atan2(y, x) - atan2(l2 sin q2, l1 + l2 cos q2) = -2.0344 + 1.0167 = -1.0177 rad. Check: the forward kinematics of (q1, q2) returns (-0.6000, -1.2000) m.
hints: The law of cosines on the triangle base-elbow-tip gives cos q2 from the distance to the target; the sign of q2 selects the elbow branch.
After q2, subtract the angle that link 2 adds to the line of sight: q1 = atan2(y, x) - atan2(l2 sin q2, l1 + l2 cos q2). Use atan2, not atan, because the target is not in the first quadrant.

cos q2 = (x² + y² - l1² - l2²)/(2 l1 l2) = -0.1253, so q2 = -acos(cos q2) = -1.6964 rad. q1 = atan2(y, x) - atan2(l2 sin q2, l1 + l2 cos q2) = -2.0344 + 1.0167 = -1.0177 rad. Check: the forward kinematics of (q1, q2) returns (-0.6000, -1.2000) m.
task.remediation: Common slips on this item: the other branch is (q1, q2) = (-3.0512, 1.6964) rad; using atan(y/x) instead of atan2 gives q1 = 2.1239 rad; reporting the world angle of link 2, q1 + q2 = -2.7141 rad, in place of the relative q2 is also wrong. Revisit the elbow branches in /lessons/R05, then practise a fresh X22 item before another independent check.

task.prompt: Planar 2R arm with relative joint angles (counter-clockwise positive; q1 is measured from the base +x axis, q2 from link 1), angles in radians, lengths in metres, everything in the base frame: l1 = 0.9 m, l2 = 0.75 m; tip position x = l1 cos q1 + l2 cos(q1 + q2), y = l1 sin q1 + l2 sin(q1 + q2). Joint limits: 2 ≤ q1 ≤ 6.2 rad and 0 ≤ q2 ≤ 2.9 rad; a joint value counts as inside its limit if it or any 2π-equivalent value is inside. The target tip position is (x, y) = (0.5, -1.0) m. Find both analytic IK solutions, count how many exist ignoring the limits and how many respect both limits, and report q1 and q2 of the admissible solution when there is one. Angles are graded modulo 2π within ±0.001 rad; you may leave angles unwrapped.
task.solution: The two analytic solutions are (-1.8387, 1.6617) and (-0.3756, -1.6617) rad, so there are 2 ignoring the limits. The pair (-0.3756, -1.6617) violates a limit even after adding or subtracting 2π, while (-1.8387, 1.6617) satisfies both (after 2π shifts where noted), so 1 solution respects the limits: q1 = -1.8387 (≡ 4.4444, inside [2, 6.2]) rad, q2 = 1.6617 rad.
hints: Compute both elbow branches first, then test each joint of each branch against its own limit, allowing a whole number of turns (2π) to be added.
For each candidate, shift q1 and q2 by multiples of 2π into the limit window if possible; a branch is admissible only when both joints fit. Count the admissible branches before reporting any angles.

The pair (-0.3756, -1.6617) violates a limit even after adding or subtracting 2π, while (-1.8387, 1.6617) satisfies both (after 2π shifts where noted), so 1 solution respects the limits: q1 = -1.8387 (≡ 4.4444, inside [2, 6.2]) rad, q2 = 1.6617 rad.
task.remediation: Common slips on this item: reporting the branch (-0.3756, -1.6617) rad that violates a limit; counting 2 solutions as admissible because both reach the target; or rejecting a joint value only because its raw value lies outside the window although a 2π-equivalent value is inside. Revisit joint limits in /lessons/R05, then practise a fresh X22 item before another independent check.

task.prompt: Planar 2R arm with relative joint angles (counter-clockwise positive; q1 is measured from the base +x axis, q2 from link 1), angles in radians, lengths in metres, everything in the base frame: l1 = 1.0 m, l2 = 0.65 m; tip position x = l1 cos q1 + l2 cos(q1 + q2), y = l1 sin q1 + l2 sin(q1 + q2). Joint limits: -4.7 ≤ q1 ≤ 0.8 rad and -2.4 ≤ q2 ≤ 2.5 rad; a joint value counts as inside its limit if it or any 2π-equivalent value is inside. For each target tip position (in m) give the number of inverse-kinematics solutions (0, 1 or 2) that respect both limits, counting configurations that differ by 2π as the same. A target on the edge of the reach band (arm fully stretched or fully folded) has exactly one configuration. A = (0.9, 0.5); B = (-0.99, 1.32); C = (0.3, -0.2); D = (-0.7, -0.8).
task.solution: Reach band: |l1 - l2| = 0.3500 m ≤ r ≤ l1 + l2 = 1.6500 m. A target on a band edge has exactly one configuration (arm straight or folded); strictly inside, two branches exist, and each must pass both limits. A: r = 1.0296 m, solutions in limits = 1; B: r = 1.6500 m, solutions in limits = 1; C: r = 0.3606 m, solutions in limits = 0; D: r = 1.0630 m, solutions in limits = 2.
hints: For each target compare the distance r = sqrt(x² + y²) with |l1 - l2| and l1 + l2 first: outside the band there is no solution, on its edge exactly one, strictly inside two.
For every target with solutions, compute q2 = ±acos(cos q2) and q1, then test each branch against both limits, adding 2π if that places a value inside. Count only the branches that pass.

task.remediation: Common slips on this item: counting a target on the edge of the reach band as two solutions (the two branches coincide there); counting both branches for a target although the limits remove one; or forgetting that a raw angle outside the window may be inside after adding 2π. Revisit reachability in /lessons/R05, then practise a fresh X22 item before another independent check.

task.prompt: A student's IK routine for a planar 2R arm computes cos q2 = (x² + y² - l1² - l2²)/(2 l1 l2), clamps it into [-1, 1], sets q2 = acos(clamped value), q1 = atan2(y, x) - atan2(l2 sin q2, l1 + l2 cos q2), and always returns the pose (q1, q2). Planar 2R arm with relative joint angles (counter-clockwise positive; q1 is measured from the base +x axis, q2 from link 1), angles in radians, lengths in metres, everything in the base frame: l1 = 1.5 m, l2 = 0.5 m, no joint limits; tip position x = l1 cos q1 + l2 cos(q1 + q2), y = l1 sin q1 + l2 sin(q1 + q2). The requested target is (x, y) = (0.3, -0.6) m. Compute cos q2 before clamping (3 decimals) and the distance in metres between the target and the tip of the returned pose (±0.001), and choose what the routine should report.
